info.title: OpenVibe.AI API
info.description: Routes of OpenVibe.AI as the OpenVibe contracts describe them (openvibe-contracts 0.269.0): each operation lists the capabilities it performs; a token for the service's audience must carry one of them unless the route is open. Generated by openvibe-contracts lib/openapi.js; do not edit.

get.summary: Read one person's Action Center items from OpenVibe.AI (plan 2026-10-28 §3.10): AI runs made on the person's behalf (on_behalf_of), as common.action-list-result@1.
get.description: **ai.actions.read** (first-party): Read one person's Action Center items from OpenVibe.AI (plan 2026-10-28 §3.10): AI runs made on the person's behalf (on_behalf_of), as common.action-list-result@1. GET /api/v1/actions?subject=usr_… with a service token; granted to OpenVibe.Network's aggregator only. Never another person's items, and only the fields of common.action-item@1.

post.summary: Run the AI operations as a developer app (ADR-014): POST /api/v1/chat, /generate, /summarize, /classify, /extract, /embed and GET /api/v1/runs/:id for the app's own runs.
post.description:
**ai.app.run** (public): Run the AI operations as a developer app (ADR-014): POST /api/v1/chat, /generate, /summarize, /classify, /extract, /embed and GET /api/v1/runs/:id for the app's own runs. The app token (sub app:app_<ULID>, project_id prj_<ULID>, env sandbox|production, audience openvibe.ai) runs as its project: every run is metered (platform.usage-sample@1 to OpenVibe.Billing, subject project:prj_<ULID>) against the project's bounded free allowance, and metered capacity is spent only under the project's tier budget; a sandbox run, and every run no tier budget governs, uses only free and local capacity. An app runs only these operations (never a workflow by key), never reads another project's runs, and never uses a person's BYO provider key.

**ai.run.create** (first-party): Create workflow runs (POST /api/v1/runs and the direct chat/generate/summarize/classify/extract/enrich/embed operations), cancel or retry the caller's own runs and attach citations to them. A token's `ns` claim limits which workflow namespaces it may run (live.*, wiki.*, ...). Quotas are checked before any provider call.

get.description: **ai.me.read** (public): The person's own AI settings (L36 Y1): GET /api/v1/me/credentials lists the provider keys they hold themselves, never a key (a four-character hint only), and GET /api/v1/me/ai/preferences reads how their runs route. A service token is refused, and so is any token carrying on_behalf_of, whatever capabilities it holds.

delete.summary: Store and change a person's memory in OpenVibe.AI (Memory M2): POST /api/v1/memory/items:batch imports up to 200 items, PATCH /items/{id} changes text, kind, scope or status, DELETE /items/{id} and DE
delete.description: **ai.memory.write** (first-party): Store and change a person's memory in OpenVibe.AI (Memory M2): POST /api/v1/memory/items:batch imports up to 200 items, PATCH /items/{id} changes text, kind, scope or status, DELETE /items/{id} and DELETE /items?source= remove rows. The person's own token or a service acting on_behalf_of them. Redaction runs again on the server (openvibe-sdk/redact), an item that is only a secret is refused, AI-produced items are suggestions until the person accepts them, and a delete removes the row (profiles that used it are rebuilt).

get.summary: Read a person's memory from OpenVibe.AI (Memory M2): GET /api/v1/memory/items, /items/{id}, /profile and /search.
get.description: **ai.memory.read** (first-party): Read a person's memory from OpenVibe.AI (Memory M2): GET /api/v1/memory/items, /items/{id}, /profile and /search. The person's own token reads their own items; a service with ai.memory.read acting on_behalf_of a person searches only the scopes its grant names (user always; project:* only for Codes runs in that project), gets active items only, at most 8, and is audited in memory_reads with item ids and never text. Suggested, archived and conflict items never reach an agent.

**ai.app.run** (public): Run the AI operations as a developer app (ADR-014): POST /api/v1/chat, /generate, /summarize, /classify, /extract, /embed and GET /api/v1/runs/:id for the app's own runs. The app token (sub app:app_<ULID>, project_id prj_<ULID>, env sandbox|production, audience openvibe.ai) runs as its project: every run is metered (platform.usage-sample@1 to OpenVibe.Billing, subject project:prj_<ULID>) against the project's bounded free allowance, and metered capacity is spent only under the project's tier budget; a sandbox run, and every run no tier budget governs, uses only free and local capacity. An app runs only these operations (never a workflow by key), never reads another project's runs, and never uses a person's BYO provider key.

ai.attribution-quota-put.v1.title: AiAttributionQuotaPut
ai.attribution-quota-put.v1.description: ai.attribution-quota-put@1 (OpenVibe.AI; roadmap WS-O task 2): a cap on runs attributed to one of the caller's own entities, PUT /api/v1/attribution-quotas/{attribution} with capability ai.quota.attribution.manage; the attribution's service must be the caller (Live caps live:user:<id>, a streamer's AI viewers). Over the cap a run is refused 429 quota.exceeded before any provider is called. Cost counts what runs have cost so far in the window, so the run that crosses the cap finishes and the next is refused.

workflow_prefix.description: Only runs of workflows whose key starts with this (live.viewers.).

ai.attribution-quota.v1.title: AiAttributionQuota
ai.attribution-quota.v1.description: ai.attribution-quota@1 (OpenVibe.AI; roadmap WS-O task 2): a cap on one attribution as its service reads it (GET or PUT /api/v1/attribution-quotas/{attribution}), with what the current window has used.

attribution.description: <service>:<type>:<id>, the run's attribution as AI keys it (Live: live:user:<id>).

ai.credential-put.v1.title: AiCredentialPut
ai.credential-put.v1.description: ai.credential-put@1 (OpenVibe.AI; roadmap WS-O task 2): a person's own provider key, stored by the service that holds their consent (Live, for a streamer's AI viewers), PUT /api/v1/credentials/{subject} with capability ai.credential.manage. OpenVibe.AI encrypts the key at rest and never returns it; runs that name the credential call that provider with it, never a shared key, and are limited by `budget_usd_per_day`. `base_url` is any https endpoint (OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic); OpenVibe.AI connects only to public addresses. Provider `node` (contracts 0.220.0) is the person's own machine instead: `machine` names it, there is no key or base_url, and a run reaches it only through OpenVibe.Bot (capability bot.machine.ai), only for that person, where they turned on "Let my AI use this computer's models".

provider.description: openai = any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. node = the person's own machine: a model on their own model server, through their OpenVibe Node and OpenVibe.Bot (no key, no base_url, no cost).

machine.description: provider node: the person's own machine (openvibe.bot/machines) whose OpenVibe Node runs the model (the ai plugin, contracts 0.219.0), or `any` (contracts 0.221.0): whichever of their machines is on, lets their AI use its models and offers the model, the fastest first, the next one when it is busy or away. Never anyone else's machine.

api_key.description: Required the first time, and whenever provider or base_url changes (a key is never sent to a new endpoint without being entered again); otherwise the stored key is kept.

models.description: Model per Live role; `chat` is the default for the others.

budget_usd_per_day.description: The person's own daily cap on estimated spend with this key; 0 or absent = no cap.

ai.credential.v1.title: AiCredential
ai.credential.v1.description: ai.credential@1 (OpenVibe.AI; roadmap WS-O task 2): a stored credential as its owner service reads it (GET or PUT /api/v1/credentials/{subject}): never the key, only its last four characters.

owner.description: The service that stored it; only it may use or change it.

machine.description: provider node: the machine it runs on, or `any` of the person's own (contracts 0.221.0)

models.description: Model per Live role; `chat` is the default for the others.

ai.definition-version-request.v1.title: AiDefinitionVersionRequest
ai.definition-version-request.v1.description: ai.definition-version-request@1: bodies of ai.workflow.manage on OpenVibe.AI. An edit is always a new version (the previous one stays readable); fields left out are taken from the newest existing version. POST /api/v1/templates/:key/versions: a prompt template (input_schema and output_schema must compile as JSON Schema; visibility public, first-party or internal). POST /api/v1/workflows/:key/versions (key <namespace>.<name>): steps (at least one; kind llm (naming an existing template), passthrough, transcribe or embed), schemas, default route, cache mode. POST /api/v1/routes/:key/versions: primary { provider, model } and fallbacks (every provider must exist), or alias_of another route. POST …/:key/versions/:version/status: { status } (templates and workflows draft|active|deprecated|archived; routes active|disabled). Refusals are 422 ai.invalid.

input_schema.description: A JSON Schema the run input must match.

output_schema.description: A JSON Schema the output must match.

ai.definition-version-result.v1.title: AiDefinitionVersionResult
ai.definition-version-result.v1.description: ai.definition-version-result@1: answers of ai.workflow.manage on OpenVibe.AI. POST …/:key/versions → 201 { template | workflow | route } (the new version, whole: prompts and schemas for a template, steps for a workflow, primary/fallbacks for a route); POST …/versions/:version/status → { template | workflow | route: { key, version, status } }.

ai.me-credential-list.v1.title: AiMeCredentialListV1
ai.me-credential-list.v1.description: ai.me-credential-list@1 (OpenVibe.AI; L36 Y1): GET /api/v1/me/credentials — every provider key the person holds themselves, without any key. Ordered by provider so a page can render it steadily.

ai.me-credential-put.v1.title: AiMeCredentialPutV1
ai.me-credential-put.v1.description: ai.me-credential-put@1 (OpenVibe.AI; L36 Y1): the person stores or replaces their own provider key at PUT /api/v1/me/credentials/{provider}. Only the person's own Network token or their AI site session may send it. `key` is required the first time and whenever `base_url` changes; a later save may leave it out to keep the stored key. The key is sealed at rest, tested on save and never returned, logged or put in an error.

provider.description: The provider. The route names it too; when both are present they must agree. A custom provider must name its endpoint in base_url.

key.description: The provider key. Required the first time and whenever base_url changes; optional afterwards, when the stored key is kept. Never returned.

base_url.description: The endpoint, for a custom provider or to override the provider's own. https only, no credentials, query or fragment; reached through the guarded fetcher's egress rules.

budget_usd_per_day.description: The person's own daily cap on this key; 0 or absent means no cap.

models.description: The model this key should use per kind of work. `auto` is not a model: absent means the provider's default, and the person's ai.me-preferences choose between keys.

ai.me-credential.v1.title: AiMeCredentialV1
ai.me-credential.v1.description: ai.me-credential@1 (OpenVibe.AI; L36 Y1): one of the person's own provider keys as the person reads it from GET /api/v1/me/credentials. It is never the key: `hint` is the last four characters, and `last_error` is a redacted line that never carries the key. `status` is what the last save-time or run-time check found: ok, failing or untested. `models_count` is how many models the provider listed when it was last tested. Own keys are free to their owner: no fee, no cap and no network budget.

hint.description: The key's last four characters, so the person can tell two keys apart. Never more.

base_url.description: The endpoint the person chose, or null for the provider's own (taken from the console presets).

budget_usd_per_day.description: The person's own daily cap on this key; null or 0 means no cap. The network's budgets never apply to their own key.

last_error.description: Why the key last failed, with the key and any other secret redacted. Never the key itself.

ai.memory-item.v1.title: AiMemoryItem
ai.memory-item.v1.description: ai.memory-item@1 (OpenVibe.AI; Memory M2): one memory item as the person's own API reads it. Tenant is the owner (`user:usr_…`); the text is decrypted only inside AI's process and never logged, never in an error, a span or an event. `source_ref` is the file path relative to the scanned root and the heading, when the item came from a file.

scope.description: `user` for the person's own notes, or `project:<slug>` for a repo or folder they chose. Never an absolute path.

text.description: The item text after the server-side redaction. Only the person's own routes and a granted agent search see it.

source.description: The adapter id (claude-code, cursor, …) or the service (actor, vibe, know, person).

source_ref.description: The path relative to the scanned root and the heading, when the item came from a file.

machine.description: The Node machine id it came from, when it came from one.

no_looks.description: True when the item was produced by an AI: the server ran noLooks on it (Memory M2 rule 5).

ai.memory-result.v1.title: AiMemoryResult
ai.memory-result.v1.description: ai.memory-result@1 (OpenVibe.AI; Memory M2): what the memory API answers: a list of items (GET /items, the batch import), one item (GET or PATCH /items/{id}), the cached profile (GET /profile), a count of deleted rows (DELETE) or the agent search's items (GET /search, at most 8, active only). The text is the person's own and is never logged.

text.description: The cached summary of the person's own notes for this scope. It passed noLooks before it was stored.

items_hash.description: sha256 of the sorted item MACs the profile was built from.

ai.memory-write-request.v1.title: AiMemoryWriteRequest
ai.memory-write-request.v1.description: ai.memory-write-request@1 (OpenVibe.AI; Memory M2): the body of POST /api/v1/memory/items:batch (up to 200 items), PATCH /api/v1/memory/items/{id} (text, kind, scope or status) and DELETE /api/v1/memory/items?source= (the source to delete). Secret shapes are redacted again on the server, and an item that is only a secret is refused. AI-produced items are suggestions until the person accepts them.

ai.model.v1.title: AiModel
ai.model.v1.description: ai.model@1: one model of a provider in OpenVibe.AI's registry (server/registry.js decodeModel): type, status, limits, per-million-token costs and what it supports.

ai.provider-manage-request.v1.title: AiProviderManageRequest
ai.provider-manage-request.v1.description: ai.provider-manage-request@1: bodies of ai.provider.manage on OpenVibe.AI. POST /api/v1/providers creates or replaces a provider (key required) and PATCH /api/v1/providers/:key changes one (fields left out keep their value); a body carrying api_key or secret is refused (422: send secret_ref env:NAME, never a secret value). POST /api/v1/models (provider_key and model_key required) and PATCH /api/v1/models/:provider/:model upsert a model. POST /api/v1/quotas upserts a quota (scope_type and window required; scope_id too unless global; the same scope, window and workflow_prefix is one quota). POST /api/v1/providers/:key/disable|enable|reset and DELETE /api/v1/cache[?workflow=] take no body. Unknown fields are ignored.

scope_id.description: * on a non-global scope = each one separately.

ai.provider-manage-result.v1.title: AiProviderManageResult
ai.provider-manage-result.v1.description: ai.provider-manage-result@1: answers of ai.provider.manage on OpenVibe.AI. Provider create/update/disable/enable → { provider } (201 on POST); POST …/reset → { health } (the circuit breaker, closed again); model upserts → { model }; POST /api/v1/quotas → 201 { quota } (the stored row); DELETE /api/v1/cache → { removed } (entries purged). Every change is audited.

ai.provider.v1.title: AiProvider
ai.provider.v1.description: ai.provider@1: one model provider as OpenVibe.AI's registry API shows it (server/registry.js publicProvider): never a secret value, only the secret reference name (env:NAME) and whether it resolves (credentials), plus the circuit-breaker health.

secret_ref.description: env:NAME, a reference; never the secret.

ai.run-citation.v1.title: AiRunCitation
ai.run-citation.v1.description: ai.run-citation@1: one source a run cited on OpenVibe.AI (the citations table): what the workflow was given or a citation the requester attached afterwards (provenance.attached), with trust and provenance.

ai.run-create-request.v1.title: AiRunCreateRequest
ai.run-create-request.v1.description: ai.run-create-request@1: bodies of ai.run.create on OpenVibe.AI. POST /api/v1/runs: ai.run-request@1. POST /api/v1/chat, /generate, /summarize, /classify, /extract, /enrich and /embed: a run of workflow ai.<op> whose input is the body itself (validated by that workflow's own input schema), except idempotency_key, target, attribution, on_behalf_of and options, which are the run's. POST /api/v1/runs/:id/citations: { citations } (1-50, each with a source_type; the requester only). POST /api/v1/runs/:id/cancel and /retry take no body.

anyOf.description: A direct operation: the workflow input fields plus idempotency_key, target, attribution, on_behalf_of and options.

ai.run-create-result.v1.title: AiRunCreateResult
ai.run-create-result.v1.description: ai.run-create-result@1: answers of ai.run.create on OpenVibe.AI. POST /api/v1/runs and the direct operations → { run, replayed? } (201 when it finished or was served from cache within the wait, 202 with Location while queued or running, 200 with replayed true for an idempotent repeat); POST …/cancel → { run }; POST …/retry → { run } (a new run with retry_of); POST …/citations → 201 { citations }. A quota refusal or a full queue is 429 with Retry-After.

ai.run-read-result.v1.title: AiRunReadResult
ai.run-read-result.v1.description: ai.run-read-result@1: answers of ai.run.read on OpenVibe.AI (the caller's own runs; usage readers may ask for all). GET /api/v1/runs?status=&workflow=&target=&limit=&before= → { runs }; GET /api/v1/runs/:id → { run, citations, requests } (the request log is metadata only: hashes, tokens, cost, latency, never prompts); GET /api/v1/runs/:id/citations → { citations }. Someone else's run is 404 run.not_found.

ai.run-request.v1.title: AiRunRequest
ai.run-request.v1.description: Body of POST /api/v1/runs on OpenVibe.AI (capability ai.run.create; ADR-015). Runs the newest active version of a workflow (or the given active or deprecated version) on input that must match that workflow version's own input schema; per-workflow input and output schemas live in AI's registry (GET /api/v1/workflows/:key), not here. The token's ns claim limits which workflow namespaces may run (403 capability.namespace_denied). ?wait=ms waits for the result: 201 finished or served from cache, 202 still queued/running (poll GET /api/v1/runs/:id), 200 an idempotent replay. Errors are problem+json: 404 workflow.not_found, 409 workflow.inactive, 409 idempotency.conflict, 413 input.too_large, 422 input.invalid, 429 quota.exceeded or queue.full with Retry-After. The direct operations POST /api/v1/{chat,generate,summarize,classify,extract,enrich,embed} take the same fields (except workflow and version) with the input fields at the top level and run workflow ai.<op>. target (EntityRef): what the output is about, part of the cache scope and a run filter. attribution (EntityRef): what the spend is attributed to for quotas and usage. on_behalf_of (SubjectRef): the person or actor the caller acts for, part of the cache scope and per-actor quotas.

version.description: Pin a workflow version (active or deprecated). Omitted: the newest active version.

input.description: Workflow input; validated against the workflow version's input_schema. Default {}.

idempotency_key.description: Same (requester, key) returns the existing run; a different workflow or input under it is 409 idempotency.conflict. The Idempotency-Key header is used when this is absent.

cache.description: false skips the scoped cache lookup and store.

debug.description: Keep raw prompts and responses in the request log, only when AI runs with raw debug logging on.

credential.description: Run with the person's own provider key (ai.credential@1) that this service stored, instead of a shared route: only that provider is called (no fallback), the result is never cached or taken from the cache, the shared paid budget is not spent, and the credential's own daily budget applies (429 quota.exceeded). Chat operations only (text, JSON, vision).

ai.run.v1.title: AiRun
ai.run.v1.description: A workflow run on OpenVibe.AI (ADR-015; server/runs.js decode): the `run` member of every run response (POST /api/v1/runs and the direct operations, GET /api/v1/runs/:id, cancel, retry) and each item of GET /api/v1/runs { runs }. Output is attributable to workflow + version + template version + route version + provider/model + run id, never to a person. A draft stays a draft: products store it with ai/ai_assisted authorship and publish nothing until a person reviews it. input keeps no inline media (replaced by data_url_sha256 and data_url_bytes) and no passthrough prompt ({ not_retained }); output is null until the run succeeded or was served from cache and then matches the workflow version's output_schema. requester is the token principal (service, app or mod). A run interrupted by a restart or shutdown ends failed with error.code run.interrupted. explain says why the run answered as it did: the task it read, the candidates it ranked and every attempt.

status.description: Terminal: succeeded, failed, cancelled, cached (a scoped cache hit, no provider call; provenance.cached_from names the run it reused).

template.description: The prompt template of the workflow's llm step; null for workflows without one.

route.description: Provider route; version null while the route is unresolved or disabled.

source_service.description: The requester's service id when the requester is a service.

code.description: run.cancelled, run.interrupted, run.internal, output.invalid, output.empty, provider.unavailable, route.unavailable, source.unavailable, media.unresolvable…

synthetic.description: Produced by the stub provider; never served to production callers and never cached.

fallback_used.description: The primary provider was degraded and the run fell back (ADR-015: fallbacks are recorded).

attempts.description: Provider calls made (skipped routes not counted).

citations_count.description: Citations stored for the run (GET /api/v1/runs/:id/citations): the sources the workflow was given, and any the requester attached later.

explain.description: Why the run answered as it did: the task-aware router's explain (L33 P3, L36 Y7). task is the requirement set it read from the request, ranked the candidates it considered and why, attempts every provider it tried with why it was chosen and why it failed, and the placement view it ranked from (objective, reasons, selected, candidates). A run that never reached a provider has no explain.

objective.description: The objective the pool planned with (cheapest, balanced, correctness, own-keys, own-machine), or null for a pinned route.

reasons.description: Why the router chose what it chose, in words.

selected.description: The provider that answered (provider, or provider/model, or the machine that answered), or null when nothing answered.

candidates.description: Every candidate the pool considered, with why it was excluded when it was.

paid_by.description: Who paid for the run: the network, the person's own key, their own machine, or a project's own provider.

task.description: The requirement set the router read off the request, with no model call.

json.description: The request asked for JSON out.

min_context.description: The context window the request needs, in tokens.

reasoning.description: How much thinking the request asked for.

ranked.description: The candidates the router ranked for this task, best first, each with its reason.

why.description: Why this candidate is here (the cheapest with vision, the strong tier, warm cache).

cost.description: The input price per million tokens, or null when the price is unknown.

tier.description: The catalogue's strength tier: fast, balanced, strong or frontier.

attempts.description: Every attempt, in order: why it was chosen, and what went wrong when it failed.

key.description: Which key or wallet paid for the attempt; never a key.

bench.description: The Bench evidence the route used, when it opted in.

usage_readings.description: The billing readings of the run, when it has any.

ai.usage-result.v1.title: AiUsageResult
ai.usage-result.v1.description: ai.usage-result@1: answers of ai.usage.read on OpenVibe.AI (all GETs, parameters in the query). GET /api/v1/status → { providers, runs, today, workflows, templates, routes, inflight, quotas }; GET /api/v1/usage?from=&to=&requester= → { usage } (daily rows); GET /api/v1/quotas → { quotas, current }; GET /api/v1/requests?provider=&status=&run=&fallback=&limit= → { requests } (request-log metadata: hashes, tokens, cost, latency; raw debug fields only for provider managers who ask); GET /api/v1/audit → { audit }; GET /api/v1/cache → { cache }; GET /api/v1/providers → { providers }; GET /api/v1/models?provider= → { models }. Never raw prompts, never secrets.

common.action-item.v1.title: ActionItem
common.action-item.v1.description: One piece of a person's agent work in the Action Center (plan 2026-10-28 §3.10): an agent task, a coding task, an AI run, or an approval waiting on them. Each authority answers its own items in this shape (common.action-list-result@1); OpenVibe.Network merges them into buckets (network.me-actions-result@1). Text is plain (no markup); a cost is what the person was charged in USD, null when unknown or free; href is a page on the authority's own public site.

service.description: The authority that owns the item.

id.description: The authority's own id (tsk_…, a Codes task id, run_…, a confirmation id, dpr_…).

title.description: A short plain-text name: the start of the task text, the workflow, or what the approval is for.

summary.description: The last step, the outcome, or what will happen on approval.

bucket.description: Where the Action Center shows it: running (queued or working), waiting (needs the person), scheduled (will run later), done, failed (failed, cancelled or expired).

state.description: The authority's own state word (queued, running, needs_you, succeeded, failed, cancelled, pending…).

agent.description: The agent, model or workflow doing it, when known.

cost_usd.description: What it cost the person, in US dollars; null when unknown or free.

steps.description: Tool calls or steps so far, when counted.

error.description: Why it failed, in words a person can act on.

next_run_at.description: When a scheduled item runs next.

href.description: The item's page: its live steps, receipt or approval.

actions.description: What the person can do from the list. approve/decline/cancel/retry go through OpenVibe.Network (POST /api/v1/me/actions/:service/:id/:action); open is a link.

common.action-list-result.v1.title: ActionListResult
common.action-list-result.v1.description: One authority's Action Center items for a person (capabilities actor.actions.read, codes.actions.read, ai.actions.read, domains.actions.read): GET /api/v1/actions?subject=usr_… with the caller's service token. Everything running, waiting or scheduled, then done and failed items from the last 30 days, newest first, at most 50.

common.entity-ref.v1.title: EntityRef
common.entity-ref.v1.description: Typed reference to another service's entity. Store this instead of a foreign key; resolve a display projection from the owner.

common.no-body.v1.title: NoBody
common.no-body.v1.description: common.no-body@1: the capability's request carries no body; its parameters are the path and query of the routes in implementedBy (an id, a page cursor). An input schema that says so explicitly, so every active capability names one (roadmap WS-C task 4).

errors.problem.v1.title: Problem
errors.problem.v1.description: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a stable OpenVibe error code and trace identifiers. The legacy 'error' string is allowed during migration so existing clients keep working.

error.description: Deprecated compatibility field: same text as title/detail for clients that read {error}.

identity.subject-ref.v1.title: SubjectRef
identity.subject-ref.v1.description: The one cross-platform reference to an actor. Issued by OpenVibe.Network. Never a service-local integer id.

oneOf.description: AgentSubject: an agent (OpenVibe.Actor, or a developer app's agent) acting under grants its owner delegated (roadmap WS-Z2). In an event envelope, on_behalf_of names the owner.

openvibeToken.description: An OpenVibe Network token for this service: a person's token, an app token (client credentials, audience of the service) or a first-party service token. Its `cap` claim must include the capability the operation names.
